assessments.title: Self-Assessments
assessments.subtitle: Standardized screenings (PHQ-9 & GAD-7) to track your wellbeing over time — your doctor sees the latest scores
assessments.questionHint: Over the last two weeks, how often have you been bothered by the following?
assessments.historyEmpty: No results yet. Complete the screening to get started.
assessments.severeHint: This score suggests significant symptoms. Please consider booking a session soon — your doctor can see this result and prepare for your visit.
assessments.savedHint: Your latest score has been saved and will appear in your doctor's pre-session briefing.
assessments.disclaimer: Screening tools are indicators, not diagnoses. Always discuss results with a qualified professional.
assessments.disclosureBody: One of your answers indicates you have had thoughts of harming yourself or dying. That is taken seriously and it has been passed to your therapist. You do not have to deal with this alone.
assessments.disclosureClinicianNotReached: We could not reach your therapist automatically just now. Please contact them directly using the numbers below or the details in your profile — this is not something to sit on.
assessments.disclosureRecorded: This was recorded so your therapist can see it before your next session.
assessments.disclosureNotRecorded: We were not able to save this to your record. Please tell your therapist directly, because they will not be able to see it.
assessments.hotlinesTitle: If you need help right now
assessments.trajectoryHint: How your screening score has moved between sittings.
assessments.trajectoryDisclaimer: This is a screening score, not a diagnosis or a measurement of recovery. A falling line means fewer symptoms were reported on that sitting; it is not proof that anything has been cured, and it does not replace a clinical assessment.

sos.title: SOS — I need help now
sos.subtitle: Alert your doctor and see crisis resources instantly
sos.confirm: This will alert your assigned doctor and show you crisis hotlines. Continue?
sos.alerted: Your doctor has been alerted. Please reach out to a crisis hotline if you need immediate support.
sos.notAlerted: We could not reach a care team. Please call one of the numbers below now — they are available 24/7.
sos.sendFailed: We could not send your alert. Please call a hotline directly.
sos.offlineFallback: You appear to be offline, so your doctor may not have been reached. Please call a hotline now.

doctorProfile.credentialsDisclaimer: A reviewed profile means an administrator at MindEase has checked the information a clinician submitted. It is not a check against a licensing board, and MindEase is not connected to one. Where a licence number is shown, it is the clinician's own statement and has not been independently confirmed. If you need a registration confirmed, ask the clinician for their registration details.
doctorProfile.scheduleNotPublished: This clinician has not published a regular schedule. Available times are shown on the booking page.
doctorProfile.scheduleMayChange: Availability may change at any time.

riskQueue.title: Risk queue
riskQueue.intro: Disclosures from your patients that may need a response today.
riskQueue.emptyHint: No unresolved risk disclosures for the patients you are treating.
riskQueue.actionFailed: That did not work. Try again.
riskQueue.newAlert: A new risk disclosure needs your attention
riskQueue.newUrgent: An urgent risk disclosure needs your attention
riskQueue.footerNote: Matches are keyword or screening signals, not clinical judgements. They exist to prompt you to look, not to act on your behalf: nothing here contacts an emergency service, and every alert is resolved by a person. Acknowledging records that you have seen it; resolving records what you did. Both are kept on the record even after the alert leaves this list.
riskQueue.loadFailed: The queue could not be loaded

safetyPlan.title: My safety plan
safetyPlan.intro: A document you write, for a moment when you may need it and cannot think clearly. Only you and the psychologist you are seeing can read it.
safetyPlan.emptyHint: You have not written one yet. It does not have to be complete - fill in what you can and come back.
safetyPlan.warningSignsHint: What you notice in yourself before things get bad. In your own words, not symptoms from a list.
safetyPlan.copingHint: What has actually worked before, as opposed to what ought to.
safetyPlan.reasonsHint: People, places, things to do. A plan that only lists problems is a hard thing to read.
safetyPlan.contactsHint: Names and numbers of people who are not clinicians. One line each.
safetyPlan.locationTitle: Where to be, and what to have to hand
safetyPlan.footerNote: This plan is yours. Nothing here is written for you, and nothing here is sent to an AI model. Your psychologist can read it so you can go through it together, and a review is recorded when that happens.
safetyPlan.loadFailedTitle: We could not load your safety plan
safetyPlan.loadFailedBody: Your safety plan was not loaded, so nothing has been changed. This is usually a temporary connection problem — try again. If it keeps happening, contact your therapist directly.

carePlan.title: My care plan
carePlan.intro: What you and your psychologist are working towards, kept between sessions so neither of you starts from scratch each time.
carePlan.newGoalPlaceholder: A goal you are working towards
carePlan.emptyHint: Add the first one. Short and specific works better than ambitious.
carePlan.actionFailed: That did not work. Try again.
carePlan.footerNote: This plan is yours. A goal you decide is no longer right can be marked dropped rather than deleted - it is useful to be able to see that something was tried and changed course.

crisis.metaDescription: If you or someone you know is in crisis, reach out now. Emergency numbers, crisis hotlines, and immediate help resources for Indonesia and international users.
crisis.title: You are not alone
crisis.subtitle: If you or someone you know is in crisis, reach out now. Help is available 24/7.
crisis.hotlinesNote: Free, confidential, and available around the clock.
crisis.reachOutBody: If talking on the phone feels hard, text or chat with someone you trust. You can also book a session with a licensed psychologist on MindEase — but if there is any immediate danger, always call first.

hotlines.name: Emergency Services (Ambulance & Police)
hotlines.note: Call immediately if there is immediate danger to life.

hotlines.name: Kemenkes SEJIWA (National Crisis Line)
hotlines.note: Kementerian Kesehatan RI — 24/7 mental health crisis line.

hotlines.name: Halo Kemenkes
hotlines.note: General health line — ask to be connected to psychological support.

hotlines.name: Into The Light Indonesia
hotlines.note: Peer support chat for those in distress (WhatsApp).

hotlines.name: Bebas Bicara
hotlines.note: Free listening ear and referral service via WhatsApp.

hotlines.name: 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline (US)
hotlines.note: For users in the United States — call or text, 24/7.

hotlines.name: Samaritans (UK & ROI)
hotlines.note: Free 24/7 helpline for anyone struggling to cope.

hotlines.name: Emergency Services (International)
hotlines.note: Standard emergency number in most countries.

steps.title: 1. Call a hotline right now
steps.description: Do not wait. Crisis lines are free, confidential, and staffed 24/7. Keep talking until you feel the immediate risk has passed.

steps.title: 2. Stay with someone
steps.description: Do not be alone if you can help it. Reach a trusted friend or family member, or go somewhere with people around you.

steps.title: 3. Remove immediate danger
steps.description: If you have access to anything that could harm you, put distance between yourself and it — or have someone you trust remove it.
